title: RBA rates to be higher for longer as oil shock adds to labour costs
full_text:
That’s all from The Australian’s rolling coverage of business and markets news for Tuesday, July 21.
Iren, the Nasdaq-listed data centre business of Aussie brothers Dan and Will Roberts surged on new contracts as investors question their lucrative share packages.
Shares in Iren surged 19.6 per cent in US trading – going against the tide on a weak day for tech stocks – after the group raised its year-end AI Cloud annualised run-rate revenue target from $US3.7bn to more than $US4bn.
Iren founders and brothers Will and Dan Roberts. Picture: Tim Hunter.
That came after it signed $US2.8bn in new customer contracts with AI developers, it told investors. Iren said 85 per cent of the ARR is now under contract following the new multi-year cloud services contracts.
IREN’s customer base now includes Microsoft, NVIDIA, Perplexity, Figure AI, Together AI, Fluidstack, Fireworks AI, Fal AI, Hume AI, and a new leading AI developer, across both bare metal and managed cloud services.
“Demand from hyperscalers, enterprises, AI developers and frontier labs continues to exceed Iren’s available and planned capacity, and Iren is engaged with customers across its entire 2026 and 2027 expansion program,” the group said.
Recent contracts also include customer prepayments representing approximately 45 per cent of the associated GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) capital expenditure, reducing Iren’s net funding requirement for those deployments.
As of June 30, Iren held approximately $US7.6bn in cash and cash equivalents.
“Our vertically integrated AI Cloud platform is scaling at pace,” Daniel Roberts, co-founder and co-CEO of Iren, said. “In the past 12 months we have expanded from approximately 3MW of self-built AI Cloud capacity to 480MW being delivered this year, with 1.2GW targeted for 2027, broadening our customer base across hyperscalers, enterprises and AI developers.”
The Sydney brothers are two of the biggest emerging names in the neocloud industry and rank among Australia’s Richest 250.
In July, Iren’s board awarded the Roberts brothers almost 9.1 million shares (as restricted stock units) in four equal instalments over the next four years, which has triggered investor disquiet.
